result.markdown: --- title: "Week 06: Comparing Groups with JAMOVI" subtitle: "Date: October 1, 2026" footer: "[course-website](https://dharaden.github.io/psyc640/)" logo: "images/640_hex.png" format: revealjs: theme: [default, brand, clean.scss] multiplex: false transition: fade slide-number: true incremental: false chalkboard: true overview: false scrollable: true code-line-numbers: true editor: visual execute: echo: true freeze: auto --- ## Today... **Groups, as lines** - Why a t-test *is* a regression (we prove it properly this time) - Dummy coding: how software turns a group into a number - Three or more groups: ANOVA is the same machine - Why not just run a bunch of t-tests? - Effect size: *d*, R², and which one to report ::: callout-note This is the **JAMOVI** version. Same data, same numbers, same conclusions as the R deck — only the buttons change. ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Where we left off Last week, in Part C of the activity: ::: incremental - You ran a **t-test** on two groups and got *t* = −2.29, *p* = .022 - You put the same grouping variable in **Factors** in Linear Regression and got **the same** *t* and *p* - The **intercept** turned out to be one group's mean, and the **estimate** the difference between the means ::: . . . Today: *why*, and what happens when there are **three** groups. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Our data: you, more or less 😴 Back to the **TIPI dataset** from Week 3 — 99 students, their personality scores, and how much they sleep. Download the TIPI data (.csv) > ☰ **Menu → Open → Browse →** `final_tipi.csv` We need a **year group** variable. In the **Data** tab: > **Compute** → new variable `year_group` → > > `IF(year_school == 1, "First year", IF(year_school == 2, "Sophomore", "Junior+"))` Then set `year_group` to **Nominal**. > **Research question:** Do students further along in school sleep differently than first-years? # Part 1: Two Groups ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Start with two Filter the sophomores out for a moment: **Data → Filters →** ``` year_group != "Sophomore" ``` > **Analyses → Exploration → Descriptives** · `hours_of_sleep` split by `year_group` | Group | N | Mean | SD | |-------------------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------| | First year | 39 | **6.13** | 1.28 | | Junior+ | 37 | **6.92** | 0.64 | Juniors and above sleep about **0.79 hours** — roughly 47 minutes — more per night. Is that more than noise? ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## The test you already know > **Analyses → T-Tests → Independent Samples T-Test** > > Dependent Variable: `hours_of_sleep` · Grouping Variable: `year_group` > > Tick **Student's**, **Welch's**, **Mean difference**, **Effect size** | Test | statistic | df | p | Mean difference | Cohen's d | |------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------| | Student's t | **−3.38** | 74 | **0.001** | −0.79 | **−0.78** | | Welch's t | −3.43 | 56.5 | 0.001 | −0.79 | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## The same question as a line > **Analyses → Regression → Linear Regression** > > Dependent Variable: `hours_of_sleep` · **Factors:** `year_group` | Predictor | Estimate | SE | t | p | |-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------| | Intercept | **6.13** | 0.164 | 37.5 | \< .001 | | Junior+ – First year | **0.79** | 0.234 | **3.38** | **0.001** | . . . ::: callout-important Same *t* (the sign just depends on which group comes first). Same *p*. The t-test is a regression with **one categorical predictor**. ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## But how do you put a *group* in an equation? $$\hat{Y_i} = b_0 + b_1X_i$$ $X$ has to be a **number**. "Junior+" is not a number. . . . So JAMOVI makes one. **Dummy coding**: | Group | coded as | |------------------|------------------| | First year (reference) | **0** | | Junior+ | **1** | That's it — and it is why the estimate is labeled **"Junior+ – First year"**. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Read the equation twice $$\widehat{sleep} = 6.13 + 0.79(junior^+)$$ ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} **First year** → plug in 0 $$6.13 + 0.79(0) = 6.13$$ The **intercept** is the mean of the reference group. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Junior+** → plug in 1 $$6.13 + 0.79(1) = 6.92$$ The **estimate** is the **difference** between the group means. ::: ::::: . . . A "line" through a predictor with two values can only ever produce **two** predicted values: the two group means. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Who is the reference group? JAMOVI uses the **first level** of the factor — alphabetically, "First year". > **Linear Regression → Reference Levels** Switch the reference to Junior+ and watch: - The intercept becomes **6.92** - The estimate flips to **−0.79** - *t*, *p*, R² and every residual **do not move** . . . Same model, different starting point. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## What about Welch? JAMOVI shows **Student's** and **Welch's** side by side. Linear Regression always assumes **equal variances** — the Student's version. . . . Look back at those SDs: **1.28** for first-years, **0.64** for juniors+. The first-years are twice as spread out. ::: callout-note That is exactly the situation Welch was built for. Here the groups are nearly the same size (39 vs 37), so the two tests agree — but with unequal *n* **and** unequal spread, they would not. Know which one you ran. ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Effect size: two flavors ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} **From the t-test panel** Cohen's *d* = **0.78** The difference in standard deviations. "How separated are the groups?" ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **From Linear Regression → Model Fit** R² = **.133** Proportion of variance in sleep accounted for by group. "How much does knowing the group help?" ::: ::::: . . . Same model. Report *d* for a two-group comparison; R² scales up to everything we do next. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 🛠️ Activity Stop 1: Same Question, Three Ways ::: callout-tip **Part A: Follow along** · \~20 min · Pairs ::: New data — the Pokémon set from your in-class check: - Run the t-test, then the regression, on the same two groups - Find the intercept in the group means - Flip the reference group and predict what will change **before** you run it [Open the activity](../class-activities/wk6_groups.html){.button target="_blank"} ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## ☕ Break {background-color="#C9ADE0"} **10 minutes** When we come back: **three** groups. # Part 2: Three or More Groups ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Put the sophomores back Turn the filter off (click the eye icon) and run Descriptives again: | Group | N | Mean | SD | |-------------------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------| | First year | 39 | **6.13** | 1.28 | | Sophomore | 23 | **6.48** | 0.90 | | Junior+ | 37 | **6.92** | 0.64 | . . . Sophomores land in the middle. Now we have **three** means — and three possible comparisons. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Why not just run three t-tests? 🤔 first-year vs sophomore · first-year vs junior+ · sophomore vs junior+ . . . Each test has a 5% false-positive rate. If the three tests were **independent**, the chance of at least one false positive would be: $$1 - (1 - .05)^3 = .143$$ . . . They are *not* independent — the three tests reuse the same three groups — so that formula overstates it a bit. Let's just **check**, by simulating studies where we **know** there is nothing to find. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 1,000 studies where nothing was going on ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lec-06_groups_JAMOVI_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: Three groups drawn from the **same** population, every pairwise t-test run, repeated 1,000 times. About **12%** of these studies produced at least one "significant" difference. None were real. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## It gets worse fast | Groups | Pairwise tests | False-positive rate | |------------------|------------------|------------------| | 2 | 1 | **4.9%** ← as advertised | | 3 | 3 | **12.3%** | | 4 | 6 | **20.2%** | | 5 | 10 | **29.2%** | [*20,000 simulated studies per row, n = 30 per group, all groups from the same population.*]{style="font-size:0.7em"} ::: incremental - The naive formula ($1-.95^{10}$ = 40% for five groups) **overstates** it, because the tests overlap - But the honest number is still **six times** the rate you think you are running ::: ::: callout-note JAMOVI has no built-in simulator, so this one is a demo rather than something to click along with. The code is on the R slides, and the activity has a version you can run if you are curious. ::: . . . This is why we start with **one** omnibus test, and why pairwise comparisons get **corrected**. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Two groups needed one dummy. Three need two. | Group | `Junior+` | `Sophomore` | |------------------|------------------|------------------| | **First year** (reference) | 0 | 0 | | Junior+ | 1 | 0 | | Sophomore | 0 | 1 | ::: incremental - $k$ groups → $k - 1$ dummy variables - Every group gets a unique pattern of 0s and 1s - The reference group is the one that is **all zeros** ::: . . . JAMOVI builds these the moment you drop a nominal variable into **Factors**. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## The model > **Analyses → Regression → Linear Regression** > > Dependent: `hours_of_sleep` · **Factors:** `year_group` > > Model Fit: tick **R²** and **Overall Model Test (F test)** **Model Fit** | R² | F | df1 | df2 | p | |------------|------------|------------|------------|------------| | **0.111** | **6.02** | 2 | 96 | **0.003** | **Model Coefficients** | Predictor | Estimate | SE | t | p | |------------|------------|------------|------------|------------| | Intercept | **6.13** | 0.159 | 38.5 | \< .001 | | Junior+ – First year | **0.79** | 0.228 | 3.47 | **\< .001** | | Sophomore – First year | **0.35** | 0.261 | 1.34 | 0.184 | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Reading it $$\widehat{sleep} = 6.13 + 0.79(junior^+) + 0.35(sophomore)$$ ::: incremental - **Intercept 6.13** = mean sleep of **first-years** (the reference) - **+0.79** = juniors+ sleep 0.79 hours more **than first-years** - **+0.35** = sophomores sleep 0.35 hours more **than first-years**, and that one is not significant - Every estimate is a comparison **to the reference group** — not to each other ::: . . . So where is sophomore vs junior+? **It isn't in this table.** JAMOVI even names the rows that way: `Junior+ – First year`. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## The omnibus F test > F(2, 96) = 6.02, **p = .003**, R² = **.111** ::: incremental - $H_0$: all three population means are equal - A small *p* says **at least one** group differs — it does not say which - This is the ANOVA you already know. Same model, different summary. ::: . . . Run it the classic way and compare: > **Analyses → ANOVA → ANOVA** · Dependent `hours_of_sleep`, Fixed Factor `year_group` > > Tick **η²** under Effect Size Same F. Same p. η² = **.111** — the same number as R². ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Getting the comparison the table hid > **ANOVA → Post Hoc Tests** > > Move `year_group` across · Correction: **Tukey** | Comparison | Mean difference | p~tukey~ | |--------------------------|--------------------------|-------------------| | First year − Junior+ | −0.79 | **0.002** | | First year − Sophomore | −0.35 | 0.377 | | Junior+ − Sophomore | 0.44 | 0.222 | ::: incremental - The omnibus test was significant because of **one** of the three comparisons - Without the pairwise step you would not know which ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Marginal means > **ANOVA → Estimated Marginal Means** Add `year_group` to a term box and tick **Marginal means plots** and **Marginal means tables**. . . . With one factor these are just the group means — but the plot (with error bars) is the figure you want in a talk, and in Week 9 these become the only sane way to read an interaction. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Writing it up > Average nightly sleep differed significantly across year in school, *F*(2, 96) = 6.02, *p* = .003, $\eta^2$ = .11. First-year students reported the least sleep (*M* = 6.13, *SD* = 1.28), followed by sophomores (*M* = 6.48, *SD* = 0.90) and juniors or above (*M* = 6.92, *SD* = 0.64). Tukey-adjusted comparisons indicated that juniors and above slept significantly more than first-year students, *p* = .002; no other pairwise comparison was significant. . . . ::: callout-tip Notice the shape: **omnibus test → group descriptives → which pairs differ**. In that order, every time. JAMOVI's tables are nearly APA already — right-click → **Export** to drop them into Word. ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## And the obvious caveat Nobody was **randomly assigned** to be a first-year. ::: incremental - Maybe upper-year students have more control over their schedules - Maybe the heavy-sleep-deprivation majors drop out before junior year - Maybe first-years live in noisier housing ::: . . . The model is fine. The **causal claim** is not available — same lesson as Lab 6. Next week's lab is the exception that proves the rule: a study where people *were* randomly assigned. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## What the model assumes ::: incremental 1. **Independence** — one row per student, no nesting (Week 13 relaxes this) 2. **Normality of the residuals** — not of the raw scores 3. **Equal variances** across groups (homogeneity) — remember SD = 1.28 vs 0.64 ::: . . . > **ANOVA → Assumption Checks** > > Homogeneity test (Levene's) · Normality test (Shapiro-Wilk) · Q-Q plot If homogeneity fails, JAMOVI offers **Welch's** correction right in the One-Way ANOVA panel. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## The big picture so far | What you want | Where it lives in JAMOVI | What people call it | |------------------|------------------------|------------------| | Continuous predictor | Regression → Linear Regression (**Covariates**) | Regression | | 2 groups | T-Tests, **or** Linear Regression (**Factors**) | t-test | | 3+ groups | ANOVA, **or** Linear Regression (**Factors**) | One-way ANOVA | | Several predictors | Covariates **and** Factors together | **Multiple regression (Week 8)** | . . . One machine. You are just changing what goes in the boxes. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## JAMOVI ↔ R cheat sheet | What you want | JAMOVI | R | |------------------------|------------------------|------------------------| | Group descriptives | Descriptives → Split by | `group_by() %>% summarize()` | | Two-group test | T-Tests → Independent Samples | `t.test(y ~ g, var.equal = TRUE)` | | Groups as a line | Linear Regression → **Factors** | `lm(y ~ g)` | | Omnibus F | Model Fit → Overall Model Test | `anova(mod)` / `summary(aov())` | | Change reference group | Reference Levels | `relevel()` / `fct_relevel()` | | Pairwise comparisons | ANOVA → Post Hoc (Tukey) | `emmeans(mod, pairwise ~ g)` | | Effect size | Cohen's d box · η² box | `effectsize::cohens_d()` · `glance()$r.squared` | | Group means plot | Estimated Marginal Means | `emmeans()` + `plot()` | | Make a grouping variable | Data → Compute → `IF(...)` | `mutate(case_when(...))` | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 🛠️ Activity Stop 2: Parts B & C ::: callout-tip **Same Question, Three Ways** · \~30 min · Pairs ::: **Part B:** three Pokémon types, from descriptives to a written-up result **Part C:** choose a reference group on purpose, and see what changes (and what doesn't) [Open the activity](../class-activities/wk6_groups.html){.button target="_blank"} ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## For next time 📋 **Lab 7 — Does the Therapy Work?**, due **Tuesday 10/6 at 11:59pm** - A real three-arm randomized trial: Individual CBT, Group CBT, Waitlist - You fit the model, pick the reference group, and write the results - Five participants dropped out — you will have to decide what to say about that 📖 Chapter 8 — ROS · Chapters 5 & 14.5 — ST · Chapter 15.4 — LSR ::: callout-note Heads up: the **midterm project** is handed out in two weeks (10/15) and due 10/27. Lab 8 is due Tue 10/13, which is during Fall Break — submit it online as usual. :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
